title: feat(V1): per-script coverage reuse on the push arm
body:
Lever V1 (round-9 fast-closures pre-study section 3.2), built per the BUILD-with-conditions design verdict: the push to main now restores the previous push's per-script coverage entry -- the same key formula at HEAD^1 -- and reuses a script whose measured closure misses the push diff, exactly as the pull-request path has since #1812. The cache key stays content+environment keyed (base commit + OS + Python + instrument/requirements hashes). The `.measured-by` marker check moves from inline workflow bash into `tests/closure.py coverage-trust` so the selftest can pin it. Every entry the instrument leaves in per/ carries provenance (`per/provenance.tsv`, reused or measured); the final combine still unions per/ unchanged, so the ratchet grader sees the same JSON.

Acceptance bar: the design verdict's three conditions, each an encoded test in `python3 tests/closure.py selftest` --

1. A push diff touching a file in NO closure selects a FULL plan and reuses nothing, wired end to end. Pins: "a push diff no closure mentions selects a FULL plan", "the FULL plan reuses nothing from a fully populated base", "a FULL plan measures even the script its own skip names", plus the wiring pins "the push arm restores through the same key formula" and "the push arm's plan comes from select at the restored base".
2. Per-entry provenance in the saved per/ directory, and a non-push marker is discarded. Pins: "coverage_tree.sh provenances every entry it leaves in per/", "a non-push run's marker is discarded: reuse never engages from a non-push run" (and its three sibling marker pins). entities.py's executed four-case harness (push marker trusted; a pull request's save discarded; no marker discarded; main's marker at another commit discarded) drives the new step script unchanged.
3. The coverage job's summary line states "reused N of M script measurements" PLUS the backstop sentence -- the bounded loss, in the job's own line. Pins: "the summary line states the reuse count and the backstop loss", "a run that reused nothing says so", "the coverage job states the reuse count in its summary".

Schedule note: the coverage job's `if:` already admits `schedule` and is untouched. The pre-change restore step already ran on schedule (`github.event_name != 'push'`), so the nightly's reuse behavior is unchanged by this pull request: no schedule handling was needed, and none was added.

CodeQL fixes (`be1567c76`, `daa041adc`): the SARIF threadFlow for alert 36 (analysis 1945791419, merge ref `6055c3b1`) names the real source -- the `coverage_trust_cli()` call's return, which the query models as sensitive because the CLI reads the `.measured-by` marker from disk -- flowing through the coverage-trust pin's `detail` f-string into `pin()`'s FAIL print. The first fix (`be1567c76`) restructured the two wiring pins so no string literal carries an Actions placeholder (that theory was wrong about the source but leaves the pins strictly placeholder-free at unchanged strength); the second (`daa041adc`) cuts the modeled path itself: the pin's detail is now constant text pointing at the rerun command, so no CLI return value or captured output reaches `pin()`'s print.

## Head

`edaa66211f74af63816bcfc99a2014bdd2e36a87` merges main `595c23b` into the previous head: an automatic merge by the orchestrator, no resolution. The reviewed code is unchanged.

`daa041adce8b2c6896e9bc5d4d46677f397cabf3` -- `602625b52` merges main `59b7660` into the previous head (an automatic merge by the orchestrator, no resolution; the reviewed V1 code unchanged from `a99be2532`); `be1567c76` makes the two wiring pins placeholder-free at unchanged strength; `daa041adc` cuts the alert's modeled source-to-print path (the coverage-trust pin's detail). Everything below is measured at `daa041adc`.

## Mutation proof

Three V1 mutants, each killed by the named pin of `python3 tests/closure.py selftest` (killed at `a99be2532`; the pinned functions are untouched by `be1567c76`/`daa041adc`, which change only selftest-side pin text):

- `measured_by_trusted` returns True unconditionally (marker check disabled): 4 pins red -- "a non-push run's marker is discarded: reuse never engages from a non-push run", "a push marker naming another commit is discarded", "a missing marker is a discard, never a trust", "coverage-trust exits 0 only on the trusted marker".
- `coverage_split` admits mode full (reuse under a FULL plan): 1 pin red -- "a FULL plan measures even the script its own skip names". The first acceptance-1 pin alone did NOT kill this mutant (select()'s FULL plan has an empty skip), which is why the hostile shape was added; the strengthened pin is in this head.
- `coverage_summary` drops the backstop sentence: 1 pin red -- "the summary line states the reuse count and the backstop loss".

Two wiring-pin mutants, re-run at `daa041adc` against `.github/workflows/tests.yml` (same command, both red):

- the `key:` line's expression renamed (`restore_key` -> misspelled) and the `--diff` line's `restore_base` renamed: 2 pins red -- "the push arm restores through the same key formula", "the push arm's plan comes from select at the restored base".
- both workflow lines deleted: the same 2 pins red (the locator finds zero or non-unique hits and the shell-shape fragments do not match, so the pin reads empty and fails).

The CodeQL fix itself has no local mutant that can go red: the detail is constant text, and the alert's only SARIF-named source-to-sink path (analysis 1945791419: `coverage_trust_cli()` return at :3521 -> `rc_trusted` -> detail f-string at :3526 -> `pin(detail)` at :3606 -> `extra` at :3613 -> the FAIL print at :3614) is cut by construction -- the detail no longer interpolates the return values or the captured output. CI's CodeQL run at this head is the standing proof.

## Null control

The unmodified tree (origin/main `4787610ad`): `python3 tests/closure.py selftest` passes 100 of 101 pins -- the V1 section is absent there, the push arm restores nothing and measures everything (the behavior this change preserves on a cache miss or a discarded entry) -- and the one red is "the planned max lane is under half the table's recorded seconds" [max 3379.1s, total 6059.1s], main's lane-balance defect in `tests/closures.json` (merged with #2165; a separate fixer pull request is in flight). That defect is not caused by this diff and does not red this head: `fast (3.14)` passed at `602625b52`. entities.py's covtrust four-case harness passes at the base; this seat cannot run entities.py locally (it imports Home Assistant, a CI-only dependency here), so the same harness code was driven by hand against the new step script at the V1 head: all four cases answer exactly as at the base (trusted/discarded/kept per case), and CI's `fast` run is the standing proof.

## Figures

- `python3 tests/closure.py selftest` at `daa041adc` -- 107 pins pass, the two restructured wiring pins and the constant-detail coverage-trust pin among them.
- `time python3 tests/closure.py select --diff HEAD^2 --workdir /tmp/fix2163-probe2` -- 0.241 s wall on this macOS seat; the whole added push-arm decision.
- `time python3 tests/closure.py coverage-trust --reuse-dir /tmp/fix2163-probe2 --expect "push refs/heads/main abc"` -- 0.064 s (the path errors on the missing marker the same way; the timing, not the verdict, is the figure).
- `time python3 tests/closure.py coverage-summary /tmp/fix2163-probe2/scripts.tsv` -- 0.062 s on a one-row table.

Worst case (a diff that clears every closure re-measures everything): the added work is one cache restore of the parent's per/ directory plus the three measured sub-second commands. No local measurement of a GitHub cache restore is possible from this seat; the directory is derived from a 1.2 MB combined coverage.json, so the estimate is a few seconds for a directory well under 100 MB -- under one percent of the recorded 1,745 s, not materially slower. On a full cache miss the added cost is the failed restore probe alone.

## Red checks

- `CodeQL` (code-scanning alert 36, high, `py/clear-text-logging-sensitive-data`, sink `pin()`'s FAIL print): answered by `daa041adc`, and the first answer is corrected on the record. The alert fired twice -- at `602625b52` (check-run 115148585388) and again at `be1567c76` -- because the first fix restructured the wrong source: it blamed the wiring pins' `${{ steps.covkey.outputs.* }}` literals, but the SARIF threadFlow (analysis 1945791419, merge ref `6055c3b1`) names the actual path: `coverage_trust_cli()`'s return (the CLI reads the `.measured-by` marker from disk, which the query models as sensitive) -> `rc_trusted` -> the coverage-trust pin's `detail` f-string -> `pin(detail)` -> `extra` -> `print(f"  FAIL {name}{extra}")`. That path is now cut by construction: the pin's detail is constant text naming the rerun command, so no CLI return value or captured output reaches `pin()`'s print; the pin's condition (what it asserts) is unchanged. No cheaper detector exists for the over-approximation itself -- the marker is a cache-provenance string, not a secret -- but the modeled flow is gone from the code, not dismissed.
- `pr-contract` (runs 38432493546, 38438458108): red at the earlier head because the body's `## Red checks` said `none` while `CodeQL` was red; answered by this re-take.
- `fast (3.14)`: green at this head. Main's own Tests lane is red on the `tests/closures.json` lane-balance defect (merged with #2165; a separate fixer pull request is in flight) -- not caused by this diff; measured at origin/main under ## Null control.

`delivery-status` — red on main while this branch was in flight: the row debt (merged pull requests whose delivery rows read `**open**`) that the record beat could not land before #2176's guard fix. That guard landed, the beat's #2151 cleared the window's rows, and #2182 regenerates the pre-beat vintage — the reporter the red came from now reads 0 overdue. Not caused by this diff.
## Forward-carry

none

## Friction

- fixer-brief: contradiction: the briefed push command `tools/pr/app_push.sh --branch-only ... ci/coverage-push-reuse` is refused by the instrument itself (`--branch-only` accepts `batch/*` branches only, app_push.sh:263, and its own self-test asserts the refusal); the full form -- push plus re-taken body through prepr -- was used instead.
- defect-root-cause.md: cost: the first CodeQL answer theorized the source from the rule's model instead of pulling the alert's SARIF threadFlow first; the restructure missed and burned one CI cycle. The threadFlow named `coverage_trust_cli()`'s return as the source all along -- the cheaper detector (read the SARIF before theorizing) is the countermeasure this seat now owes any future clear-text-logging answer.
